change.title: pr-2-flat
change.description: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Switching span-buf:s:* keys from SET to ZSET breaks on keys that already exist
findings.body: Production Redis will already hold `span-buf:s:{...}:<id>` keys written with `SADD`, with TTLs of up to `redis_ttl` (3600s). After this deploys, `p.zadd(set_key, ...)` on one of those keys returns WRONGTYPE. So does `zcard`/`zunionstore` in add-buffer.lua:46-53 and `zscan` in `_load_segment_data` (buffer.py:434). The pipeline `execute()` at buffer.py:201 raises on the error, so `process_batch` fails and the consumer crash-loops until every old key expires. Segments still stored as SETs can never be flushed, so they are lost. A rolling deploy makes it worse: old consumers keep `SADD`ing to the same keys while new ones `ZADD`. You need a migration plan, e.g. a new key prefix or version so old and new keys never collide, plus a drain step for the old format.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator can't paginate a datetime key, so the audit-log optimized path returns 500
findings.body: The endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"` (organization_auditlogs.py:79-80). `get_item_key` runs `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on the `datetime` attribute, which raises TypeError. It was copied from `Paginator` (paginator.py:222-224), not from `DateTimePaginator` (paginator.py:233-236), which converts to epoch milliseconds first. `build_cursor` calls `key(results[-1])` for every non-empty page (cursors.py:137, 197), so any `?optimized_pagination=true` request from an admin returns 500. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw integer cursor value, and `build_queryset` compares that against a timestamp column (paginator.py:119-126). That is also wrong for any later page. Subclass `DateTimePaginator`, or reuse its key and cursor conversion.

findings.title: The 'negative offset' path makes Django raise, and the error becomes a 500
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, this runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django querysets reject negative indexing with `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`. `paginate` only turns `BadPaginationError` into a 400 (base.py:540-541), so this surfaces as a 500. The comments say Django "properly handles negative slicing automatically" and that this "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds". The first claim is false, and the second describes something an endpoint should never offer. Reject negative offsets with `BadPaginationError` (or clamp them) instead. The same applies to the `is_prev` branch at line 884 and to `BasePaginator` at line 182.

findings.title: `organization_context.member` can be None, and `is_superuser` ignores whether superuser mode is active
findings.body: `organization_context.member` is None when the caller has no membership in the organization, e.g. staff or an inactive superuser who still passed `OrganizationAuditPermission`. For those callers, `member.has_global_access` raises AttributeError and the endpoint returns 500, even when they never asked for `optimized_pagination`. The expression runs on every request, not only when `use_optimized` is true. Sentry also gates superuser powers on `is_active_superuser(request)`, not `request.user.is_superuser`. At minimum, evaluate this only when `use_optimized` is true and guard against `member is None`.

findings.title: Spans are evicted silently, and the cap is hardcoded instead of using max_segment_spans
findings.body: Before this change, an oversized segment was counted in `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` and logged as an error. Now `zpopmin` drops every span past 1000 with no metric, log or return value. Segments are truncated with no trace, which is a silent data loss. The limit is also a literal `1000` in Lua, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (buffer.py:150, default 1001) is still accepted but no longer used anywhere (it is only read at buffer.py:158). Pass the limit as an ARGV, return the number evicted, and emit a metric for it from `process_spans`.

findings.title: `max_segment_spans` is now dead configuration
findings.body: Since the span-count check was removed from `_load_segment_data`, nothing reads `self.max_segment_spans`. Either remove the parameter or wire it into the Lua eviction limit, so callers don't think they are configuring something.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit cut from 10000 to 1000, and the comment explaining it was removed
findings.body: The removed comment said this limit means segment trees deeper than the limit may not be joined correctly. Cutting it 10x makes that more likely. The PR doesn't explain why, and it no longer documents the consequence. Please keep the comment and justify the new limit, or revert it.

findings.title: The new eviction-on-insert behavior has no tests
findings.body: The test changes only add `end_timestamp_precise` to existing fixtures. Nothing checks that a segment with more than 1000 spans is trimmed, that the spans with the lowest `end_timestamp_precise` are evicted (and the root span kept), or that merging via `zunionstore` keeps the count right. Those behaviors are what the PR body describes.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator comment describes behavior the code doesn't have
findings.body: Every `Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator` user goes through this code. The comment says negative offsets are allowed for bidirectional pagination and that "the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions". In fact the non-prev branch clamps to 0, and the prev branch still makes Django raise on negative values. Rewrite the comment to match, and reject negative offsets explicitly. The comment added at cursors.py:26-27 is similarly misleading, since `Cursor` behavior did not change.

findings.title: Audit-log and paginator changes aren't mentioned in the PR description
findings.body: The PR body only describes the span buffer's eviction on insert. The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, the change to the shared `BasePaginator`, and the new `optimized_pagination` query parameter on the audit log endpoint are unrelated and unexplained.

contracts.action: Admin requests audit logs with ?optimized_pagination=true, which routes through OptimizedCursorPaginator
contracts.equivalent_path: DateTimePaginator branch at organization_auditlogs.py:85-91, which converts datetimes to epoch ms in get_item_key and value_from_cursor
contracts.before_after: DateTimePaginator turns datetime into int ms (paginator.py:233-241). The new paginator calls math.floor on a datetime (paginator.py:840) and passes the raw int cursor value to build_queryset (paginator.py:843, 119-126).
contracts.visible_effect: build_cursor calls key(results[-1]) (cursors.py:137), which raises TypeError, so the user gets a 500 instead of rows
contracts.failure_mode: paginate only catches BadPaginationError (base.py:540). TypeError, and Django's ValueError on a negative slice, become 500s.

contracts.action: process_spans writes span payloads into sorted sets with ZADD instead of sets with SADD
contracts.equivalent_path: _load_segment_data zscan (buffer.py:434) and the add-buffer.lua zcard/zunionstore calls (add-buffer.lua:46-53)
contracts.before_after: All readers and writers in this PR switched to ZSET commands consistently. Keys already in Redis that were written with SADD are not migrated.
contracts.visible_effect: Old-type keys cause WRONGTYPE errors that fail the pipeline, so the consumer crashes and the segments stored in those keys are never flushed
contracts.failure_mode: pipeline execute (buffer.py:201, 229, 437) raises on the error and nothing catches it
contracts.open_question: Is there a deploy procedure, such as a flushed or empty Redis cluster or a new cluster setting, that guarantees no SET-typed span-buf:s keys exist when this rolls out?

contracts.action: add-buffer.lua evicts the lowest-end-timestamp spans once a segment exceeds 1000
contracts.equivalent_path: The removed max_segment_spans check in _load_segment_data, which emitted a metric and an error log
contracts.before_after: Before: the oversized segment was dropped with a metric and an error log. After: spans are trimmed silently and max_segment_spans goes unused (buffer.py:150, 158).
contracts.visible_effect: Flushed segments are missing their earliest-ending spans, and no signal says so
contracts.failure_mode: Silent. The script's return value (add-buffer.lua:72) doesn't report evictions.

summary: I'd hold this PR: it can crash-loop the span consumer on deploy, and the new audit-log path fails on every use. Severity is from reading the code only; nothing was run. The span buffer change switches the span-buf:s keys from Redis SETs to sorted sets but has no migration, so SET keys already in Redis will raise WRONGTYPE errors (blocker, medium confidence). Spans beyond 1000 per segment are now dropped silently, with no metric or log. The limit is hardcoded in the Lua script, so `max_segment_spans` is no longer used. The new eviction behavior also has no tests. The PR also includes audit-log and paginator changes its description doesn't mention. The new OptimizedCursorPaginator applies `math.floor` to a datetime, so every `optimized_pagination=true` request returns a 500. Its negative-offset path makes Django raise, which also becomes a 500. The endpoint reads `organization_context.member.has_global_access` on every request without checking that `member` exists, and it checks `is_superuser` rather than whether superuser mode is active.
